title: Predictive Burst Cache Coordinator - PRD Brief
body:
Purpose:
This note captures an early PRD for a Predictive Burst Cache Coordinator (PBCC) — a platform-level component that coordinates proactive prefix/KV cache warming and short-lived warm-pools across Dedicated capacity to reduce cold-start token latency during microbursts and to minimize cost of throttled overprovisioning.

Context / problem we see:
- Tenants experience long-tail latency spikes when sudden short-lived load occurs (chat spikes, seasonal events).
- Current mitigation options: keep larger reserved capacity (expensive) or rely on burst credits (works but causes cold KV cache misses and latency tails).
- Autoscalers react too slowly for microbursts (seconds-to-minutes). Filling KV cache at request time produces poor p99s.

High-level idea:
- PBCC predicts imminent bursts for each tenant using short-window telemetry (request rate deltas, recent retry spikes, webhook triggers) and then coordinates targeted cache pre-warming across the Dedicated fleet.
- Two working levers: 1) short-lived warm-pools (ephemeral GPU-backed contexts with preloaded KV/prefixs) and 2) cross-tenant cooperative prefix snapshotting + synth-prefetch (for tenant-allowed preloads).
- PBCC operates within tenant isolation constraints (never loads customer private data unless allowed by config). Default: only model-agnostic or customer-consented prompt artifacts are preloaded.

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce p99 generation latency for microbursts (<60s duration) by >=40% for targeted tenants.
- Reduce cold-start token penalty measured as added token time by >=50% vs baseline.
- Keep warm-pool cost delta under 8% of customer monthly Dedicated spend for participating tenants.
- No cross-tenant leakage or privacy violations; audits enabled.

Core components / behavior:
1) Burst signal detector: lightweight rules + ML score (delta rps, route anomalies, scheduled jobs, external signals via webhook). Emits predictions with confidence and TTL.
2) Cache warming planner: given predictions, chooses warm-pool size, which prefixes/kv-slices to preload, and where to allocate (locality-aware: same region / nearest pool). Considers tenant's reserved capacity and burst-credit budget.
3) Warm-pool orchestrator: orchestrates ephemeral contexts (minutes) with preloaded caches and optional quantified quantization profiles to speed token generation.
4) Fallback & grace policies: if warm-pool creation fails or costs exceed thresholds, degrade to lighter prefetch (cold KV caches with sampled prefetches) and notify routing layer to apply soft-latency SLO adjustments.
5) Audit & consent manager: config knobs for tenant: \"allow-prefetch\": {none, model-only, all-prompts}, logging level, retention. Integrates with KMS policy and Private deploy constraints.

Isolation and safety controls:
- Each warm-pool is single-tenant or runs with encrypted ephemeral cache shards; never share raw KV payloads across tenants.
- Resource quota gating: PBCC respects reservation commitments and only borrows opportunistic capacity when explicit overcommit policies are enabled.
- Cost circuit breaker: global and per-tenant thresholds stop prewarming if projected cost > X% of monthly burn (configurable).
- Observability: per-prediction trace id, prewarm duration, cache-hit delta, cost of warm-pool creation, and p99 improvement.

Autoscaling integration:
- PBCC acts as a short-horizon autoscale hint provider. It can request ephemeral contexts instead of changing long-lived pool sizes; it may also nudge the platform autoscaler to temporarily add capacity when predictions show multi-minute sustained growth.
- Provide simple API: POST /v1/pbcc/hint {tenant_id, expected_rps, window_seconds, priority}. Hints are optional; platform retains final allocation decision.

Operational runbook (rough):
- On repeated warm-pool failures: reduce prediction sensitivity, notify tenant via console, pause warm-pools for that tenant.
- During global capacity pressure: PBCC degrades to sampling-only prefetch and emits telemetry for product ops.
- Testing plan: staged rollout on internal tenants, then opt-in customers with low blast radius and explicit cost caps.

Privacy & compliance notes:
- For Private deployments: default is consented-only prewarming; PBCC must run inside customer VPC control plane.
- Logging: PII scrubbed or hashed; retain traces for 30 days by default.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Prediction model: start with rule-based + lightweight XGBoost on 10s-30s features; timeline: prototype in 6 weeks.
- Prefetch content scope: for chat, should we simulate typical prefixes or only cache model KV state (avoid caching customer prompts unless consent)? Need legal review.
- Billing model: do we bill warm-pool minutes separately, as a separate metered add-on, or include within Dedicated burst credits? Product: recommend separate metered line with monthly cap.
- Failure modes: what if prewarming improves p99 but increases tail enqueue times due to resource contention? Need simulation harness.
- UX: console toggles for per-route PBCC opt-in and per-tenant cost cap.

Experiment proposal (MVP):
- Phase 0 (internal): Collect telemetry, implement rule-based detector, and attach a no-op planner that records hypothetical prewarm decisions.
- Phase 1 (opt-in beta): Implement planner + warm-pool orchestrator; offer ~20 internal tenants opt-in with strict cost caps; measure p90/p99 improvements and cost delta.
- Phase 2 (graduation): Expose console toggles, API hints, and integrate with Dedicated billing.

Appendix (quick checklist):
- [ ] Prototype detector (2 weeks)
- [ ] Simulate prewarm cost vs benefit using historical traffic (1 week)
- [ ] Implement warm-pool lifecycle (3 weeks)
- [ ] Add consent/audit controls and console UI mock (2 weeks)
- [ ] Legal signoff for prompt prefetch scope (TBD)

Notes to reviewers: This doc is a working brief — aim is to capture a bounded, testable lever that reduces microburst latency without forcing full overprovisioning. Looking for feedback on privacy model, billing approach, and acceptable isolation guarantees.
